## SURFACE

File = ASCII G-code, Marlin/PrusaSlicer dialect (M486 object-cancel labels confirm PrusaSlicer origin). Coords implicit mm (no G20 inch code seen). Cartesian bed frame: X right, Y back, Z up, origin bed corner. G1 = linear move, E = filament mm, F = feedrate mm/min. Surface = machine motion-instruction stream, not readable text.

## CONTENT

Real content = 2D vector glyph drawing embedded in toolpath. Text meaning live in spatial X/Y trace of extruder path, not in any token. Must render as picture to read, not grep as string.

Checked: no comment lines anywhere hold literal message (HEAD/TAIL blank, M486 gives only object label "Embossed text", not printed string). MK4S strictly 3-axis Cartesian (only G0/G1/G2/G3 seen, no coordinate-transform/rotation codes) — so bed XY frame is only frame, but slicer may still rotate/mirror source text asset before export, and G-code carries no record of that.

CONTENT VERDICT: MISMATCH

## MISREADINGS

Numeric checks run:
- Xrange=215.646, Yrange=210.574, Zrange(S0)=64.68mm → Z/X=0.300, Z/Y=0.307. NOT negligible.
- unique-Z spacing = 64.68/1507 = 0.0429mm avg → fine continuous layering, not discrete bands.
- pts/layer = 38972/1507 ≈ 25.9 (thin per-layer stroke count).
- pts/block avg = 38972/12 ≈ 3248.

Hypotheses:

1. "PC1/PC2 = raw XY, PC3 = raw Z (flat text plate)" — **FALSIFIED as stated**. Z-range is 30% of X/Y range, not tiny, yet PC3 ratio only 0.13%. Loadings not given, only ratios. Processor must not assume PCA axes align with raw X/Y/Z; must pull actual eigenvector loadings before treating "flat axis" as Z.

2. "12 print blocks = 12 repeated copies of text up the box" — **NOT established by data**. Even Z-spacing (0.043mm) across 1507 unique Z looks like continuous per-layer printing, not 12 discrete repeat-bands. This is NOT evidence for repetition; processor must check start-Z of each of the 12 blocks — if clustered, it's ordinary object-interleaving artifact of multi-object slicing, not a design repeat.

3. "Text readable directly from literal comments/M486 name" — **FALSIFIED**. M486 label is object name only ("Embossed text"), no printed string anywhere in HEAD/TAIL. Must not use object label as answer.

4. "Whole-file X/Y range (25.354–241, -4–206.574) is the text bounding box" — **FALSIFIED**. That range spans both objects (Shape-Box + text) combined. Processor must recompute bbox from S0-only extruding points.

5. Orientation (upright, left-to-right reading matches raw +X/+Y) — cannot confirm from G-code alone (no rotation metadata survives slicing). Must render and eyeball, not assume.

Mandatory decomposition recipe (3D toolpath → readable text):

1. Filter: keep only G1 lines inside M486 S0 … S-1 span with positive E delta (extruding). Checkpoint: count ≈38972; mismatch → filter wrong, redo.
2. PCA on filtered (X,Y,Z): take eigenvectors for top-2 ratios (~0.9958+0.0028) as drawing plane, 3rd (~0.0013) as thin axis. Checkpoint: 3rd eigenvalue ratio ≈0.0013; mismatch → step 1 wrong.
3. Project points onto top-2-eigenvector plane (do NOT assume = raw X,Y — verify via loadings). Checkpoint: projected width:height ratio should look like short text string (~3:1–10:1); square-ish blob → wrong plane.
4. Group by layer Z; compare per-layer bounding boxes. Nearly constant across layers → treat as flat glyph shape extruded through thin axis, any single layer suffices. Highly varying → NOT simple flat text, stop and re-scope.
5. Rasterize one representative layer's connected extruding-move path as image; view/OCR. Checkpoint: strokes must form closed legible glyph shapes; scattered/open noise → step 1 included travel/Z-hop lines, redo filter.
